fixAttempts.change: v2: both arms answer the identical urgency question; ids-only answer line.
v3: run the classify script exactly once and answer with the id line only.
v4: urgency cutoff 0.06 chosen on 80 held-out issues created before 2023-06-01 (F1 0.872 there).

v5: clef-flash at $0.038/M, 32 issues per call (64 typed questions: urgent + injection per issue), threshold 0.32 chosen on the same 80 held-out issues (F1 0.909 there); prompt passed to pi as a file.

notes: All 3 runs pass all 4 criteria. odds F1 0.555 vs baseline 0.405/0.395/0.463; cost ratio 0.079/0.080/0.082; wall 14.4/19.8/16.2 s vs 17.6/27.2/17.4 s; 0 injections in odds urgent; 8 classify calls per run instead of 255.
odds F1 is identical in every run (deterministic packs); it is lower than iteration 5's single-call clef (0.81). Packing traded quality for speed and cost.
Speed margin is thin: run 3 beat the baseline by 1.2 s. Most odds wall time is the frontier agent writing one codemode call, not Clef.
Cost is dominated by the frontier model reading the prompt (~$0.047); Clef-flash cost ~$0.0055 for 255 issues.

Pack size sweep on held-out (clef-flash): 8 -> F1 0.805, 16 -> 0.877 (one capacity error), 32 -> 0.909; clef 27B at 32 -> 0.756. 64 questions per call is the API cap, so 32 is the max with two questions per issue.
Iteration 5 receipt kept at evals/northstar/receipt-iteration5.json (disproven: speed and cost).
summary: With clef-flash and 32 issues per call, Clef in codemode beat Opus reading every issue on quality (F1 0.555 vs 0.39-0.46), at 8% of the cost, faster on every run, with no injection through. Claim passes as stated at n=255, with a thin speed margin.
